slides.title: 18.1.2 Using Member Initializer Lists
keyPoints: A member initializer list follows the constructor’s parameter list and initializes base classes and members before.
Use it to initialize members directly rather than default-constructing them and assigning later.
Const members and references require appropriate initialization rather than later reseating.
A member initializer list follows the constructor’s parameter list and initializes base classes and members before.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use 18.1.2 Using Member Initializer Lists as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. A member initializer list follows the constructor’s parameter list and initializes base classes and members before the constructor body runs. Use it to initialize members directly rather than default-constructing them and assigning later. Const members and references require appropriate initialization rather than later reseating. Actual member construction follows declaration order in the class, not the order written in the initializer list. Keep the written order consistent with declaration order to avoid misleading readers and compiler warnings. Do not initialize an earlier member from a later member that has not yet been constructed. If dependencies are complicated, reconsider the representation or compute validated inputs before construction. slides.title: 18.2.2 Providing Sensible Default Values
keyPoints: Default member initializers and default constructors reduce uninitialized state, but a default should have a real.
Zero quantity is sensible for an empty stock count.
A fake network port or an empty required credential may create a misleading object that cannot perform its.
Default member initializers and default constructors reduce uninitialized state, but a default should have a real.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use 18.2.2 Providing Sensible Default Values as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Default member initializers and default constructors reduce uninitialized state, but a default should have a real domain meaning. Zero quantity is sensible for an empty stock count. A fake network port or an empty required credential may create a misleading object that cannot perform its advertised role. When no useful default exists, require the necessary parameter or represent the absence explicitly with a separate type. Do not invent a magic invalid value merely to make default construction possible. A type that cannot be default-constructed can be easier to use correctly than a type that silently begins in an undocumented unusable state. slides.title: 18.3.1 Understanding Destructor Execution
keyPoints: A destructor runs as a class object’s lifetime ends through ordinary scope exit, deletion by an owner, or other.
Local objects are destroyed in reverse order of completed construction.
This ordering lets an inner helper finish before the outer context it depends on is destroyed.
A destructor runs as a class object’s lifetime ends through ordinary scope exit, deletion by an owner, or other.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use 18.3.1 Understanding Destructor Execution as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. A destructor runs as a class object’s lifetime ends through ordinary scope exit, deletion by an owner, or other specified lifetime-ending operations. Local objects are destroyed in reverse order of completed construction. This ordering lets an inner helper finish before the outer context it depends on is destroyed. Do not promise destructor execution after every conceivable process failure. Abrupt termination, certain fatal signals, or power loss do not provide normal stack unwinding. Destructors are a language-level cleanup mechanism, not a replacement for durable storage protocols or external recovery. Also avoid allowing cleanup destructors to throw during stack unwinding, because that can terminate the process. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use Requirement and simplest approach as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. HarborWorks needs a quantity that is valid immediately after construction and a visible demonstration that completed local objects are cleaned up when their scopes end. A tempting shortcut is to provide an empty constructor plus a setter and hope every caller remembers to invoke the setter. That creates a state that the type does not need and distributes responsibility across callers. The selected design makes the quantity constructor enforce the interval. A separate lifetime probe observes scope behavior without confusing the domain quantity with a fake external resource. slides.title: Trace the implementation
keyPoints: The default quantity delegates to the validated constructor.
The explicit keyword prevents unintended implicit conversion from an integer in contexts where that would obscure.
Invalid construction throws, and the test catches that specific exception to confirm rejection.
LifetimeProbe borrows a counter that outlives both probes.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use Trace the implementation as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. The default quantity delegates to the validated constructor. The explicit keyword prevents unintended implicit conversion from an integer in contexts where that would obscure the domain operation. Invalid construction throws, and the test catches that specific exception to confirm rejection. LifetimeProbe borrows a counter that outlives both probes. Construction increments it and destruction decrements it. Copying is disabled because an implicit copy would not perform the increment while its destructor would still decrement, breaking the counting invariant. This is a preview of why resource-like classes need deliberate special-member behavior. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 18, use Evidence and interpretation as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. The printed live count of zero is the final observation. slides.narration: Use this checkpoint as a pressure test. The learner should answer before seeing the provided explanation: What does a constructor establish? The supplied answer is: It initializes a new object's bases and members and must establish the required valid state before successful construction finishes.. Do not let the session end with memorized phrasing. Ask for the evidence. In this chapter, evidence means source-level mechanism, runtime output, diagnostic behavior, preserved state, or an acceptance condition.
actions: Give learners thirty seconds to answer before opening the details disclosure.
When revealing the answer, require one sentence of evidence, not just the label of the concept.
Connect the answer back to the chapter's code or acceptance boundary.

slides.title: Close the lecture with evidence
keyPoints: Restate the chapter contract

Assign a small edit-and-explain task
slides.narration: Close Chapter 18 by having learners restate the chapter in one engineering sentence. For Controlling Object Construction and Destruction, that sentence should include the mechanism, the boundary, and the evidence. Then ask for the thing most likely to fool a beginner: confusing a printed value with correctness, ignoring stderr, assuming exit status proves output, or trusting a diagram without checking code. The homework move is small but serious: make one controlled change, predict the new output, run it, and write the explanation in terms of source behavior.
actions: Return to the chapter Outline and point learners to Code & labs for the source files.
Assign one controlled edit to the interactive lab and require a written output explanation.
Tell learners to export lecture work if they modified code during the session.
